title: CGAZ Name Search Index
description: A search sidecar, not a boundary dataset: one row per named administrative unit across all three CGAZ levels, 52,398 rows in 3.6 MB, sorted by a folded form of the name. The sort is the whole design. The intended use is to load the file whole, which at this size takes a couple of hundred milliseconds in a browser; row group statistics on `name_norm` are tight, non-overlapping alphabetical ranges, so a client that will not load 3.6 MB can instead resolve a typed prefix from one or two 101 KiB row groups by HTTP range request. Each row carries the `shapeID` that joins it back to the boundary collection for its level, a bbox to fly a map to, a point inside the unit, and how many other units share the same name. The [agent guide](AGENTS.md) has both lookup recipes and the join back to geometry.

providers.name: geoBoundaries, William & Mary geoLab
providers.description: The geoBoundaries Global Database of Political Administrative Boundaries, built by the community and William & Mary geoLab. CGAZ composites country submissions against US Department of State international boundaries.

providers.name: Portolan Mirrors
providers.description: Republishes the CGAZ release as cloud-native GeoParquet and PMTiles. Adds no boundaries and changes no geometry.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: The unit's name exactly as geoBoundaries publishes it, including the 38 rows whose upstream text is double-encoded UTF-8. Display this; search name_norm.

table:columns.name: name_norm
table:columns.description: Derived, and the column the file is sorted by. The name lowercased with Unicode case folding and with combining accent marks stripped through NFKD, so 'Zurich' finds 'Zürich'. The 38 double-encoded upstream names are repaired here first, so 'region de valparaiso' finds the row whose published name is 'RegiÃ³n de ValparaÃ­so'. Scripts with no Latin decomposition, such as Han, are lowercased and otherwise unchanged.

table:columns.name: level
table:columns.description: 0, 1 or 2: which boundary collection holds this unit's geometry. 218 rows at level 0, 3,202 at level 1, 48,978 at level 2.

table:columns.name: shape_type
table:columns.description: ADM0, ADM1, ADM2 or DISP, from the boundary row. Every row's shape_type matches its level, because the index takes each unit only from the file that level natively belongs to; DISP rows sit at level 0.

table:columns.name: country
table:columns.description: The boundary row's shapeGroup: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, or a geoBoundaries disputed-area code 111 to 129. Also the join key back to the ADM0 collection for level-0 rows.

table:columns.name: country_name
table:columns.description: Derived. The ADM0 shapeName for this row's country, joined on shapeGroup, so an autocomplete can show 'Zurich, Switzerland' without a second fetch. NULL for the 20 disputed areas, which have no ADM0 parent.

table:columns.name: shape_id
table:columns.description: The boundary row's shapeID, and the join key back to the ADM1 or ADM2 collection. NULL for every level-0 row, because CGAZ ADM0 publishes no shapeID; join those on country instead.

table:columns.name: area_km2
table:columns.description: Derived. The unit's geodesic area in square kilometres, copied from its boundary row and rounded to three decimals. Useful as a relevance weight: of two units with the same name, the larger is usually the one meant.

table:columns.name: name_dupes
table:columns.description: Derived. How many rows in this index share this row's name_norm, counted worldwide and across levels. 1 for 44,258 rows; 878 rows sit in a name shared by 10 or more units, and 32 units are called Washington. An autocomplete needs this to decide when to disambiguate.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 bbox covering struct, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax in CRS84: the unit's full extent, copied from its boundary row. This is what to fly a map to after a hit. Stored as float32 rather than float64 to halve what it costs in a file meant to be loaded whole, with every bound rounded outward so the box still contains the unit. Verified against the ADM2 collection: 0 of 48,978 joined rows have a bbox narrower than their true extent. Precision is about 1e-5 degrees, roughly a metre. The boundary collections keep float64.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Derived. A Point as WKB in CRS84, from ST_PointOnSurface of the unit's polygon, so it is guaranteed to fall inside the unit rather than outside it the way a centroid can. Use it for a marker, not as the unit's geometry.

index-manifest.title: Index manifest for the geocoder (cnmw-index/1.0)
index-manifest.description: The kilobyte a client fetches before the index: its size, row group count, checksum, catalog version, the URL and row count of every boundary and display file, and the attribution each one requires with a share_alike flag. Also documents the level-0 join (country/shapeGroup, no shapeID) and the absent cnmw:catalog_version footer metadata.
